traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md describes an optional ESLint rule that recommends migrating from legacy `@story`/`@req` annotations to the new `@supports` format, with conservative auto-fix support and configurable severity. The implementation matches this specification:
- The new rule `prefer-implements-annotation` is implemented in src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts with clear traceability to this story and its REQ IDs. - It detects combined `@story` + `@req` usage, warns by default only when explicitly enabled, and remains disabled in the built-in recommended/strict presets to preserve backward compatibility. - Auto-fix behavior is deliberately constrained to simple single-story patterns and produces a single `@supports` line combining all requirement IDs while preserving JSDoc formatting and order; more complex or mixed patterns are reported with clear messages (`cannotAutoFix`, `multiStoryDetected`) and no fix. - Legacy-only comments (`@story`-only, `@req`-only, `@supports`-only) remain valid and unaffected, both by rule design and by tests explicitly confirming no diagnostics. - Tests in tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts cover all main requirements: optional warning, single- and multi-requirement auto-fixes, multi-story/mixed detection, conservative behavior for complex annotations, and configuration behavior. These tests are executed by the Jest suite and all pass. - Documentation includes both a detailed rule page and a user-facing migration guide with configuration examples and explanations of when and how to use the rule.
The only minor issue found is a small typo in the rule doc’s `@story` reference path (`MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS` vs `MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS`), which affects internal traceability metadata but not user-visible behavior or the acceptance criteria. Given that all functional and documentation acceptance criteria for this story are met and validated by passing automated tests, the story is assessed as PASSED.
